answers.core: Because movement is important, and decreasing fidelity that can be achieved by mid-level and high-level functions looks wrong. It can be in the asset library, or it can be left like it is, but then it can turn a lot of people from Godot. Beginner-friendly should not mean beginner-only, or rather beginners + those who ready to dive at the level of engine developer, understand how move_and_slide works (by the looks of it it's rather complicated) and make their own.
answers.workaround:
It will be used quite often. However, yes there is one, but ugly, workaround - apply small movement into surface with another move_and_slide after each step with main one. That messes with slides count, is_on_floor/wall/ceiling conditions and requires to retrieve and copy intermediate data in script, each step, which probably can be costly.
On the other hand, making similar functionality by the means of move_and_collide and low-level stuff is hard. It can work, but there is too many corner cases, and forcing regular game developer to do that is too much.

title: Make it possible to use move_and_slide in user implemented character controllers, not only in premade one in Godot 4, and maybe some improvements for more advanced use
